newsitem.title: CHINA: China yuan June interbank market turnover falls.
newsitem.headline: China yuan June interbank market turnover falls.

text.p: The Shanghai-based China local currency interbank market traded 46.658 billion yuan in June, down from 59.889 billion yuan in May, the China Securities newspaper said on Monday.
Average daily turnover was 2.22 billion yuan, down from 2.852 billion yuan, the newspaper said.
The weighted average rate for the seven contracts traded on the market edged up 0.026 percentage points to 11.13 percent, it said. It gave no details.
Trading was less active in June after Beijing took a series of crackdown measures on the financial markets, casting uncertainty on the interbank market, traders said.

Among the measures was a ban by the People's Bank of China on state banks trading state debt contracts on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges and regional state debt trading centres to prevent bank money from flowing into the stock markets.
The central bank ordered the banks to shift their state debt trading to the interbank market.
"The official crackdown measures have cast some uncertainties on the interbank market making trading dull, especially in the second half of June," one trader said.
"But in the long run, the measures will help standardise the market and volume will pick up as a result," he said.
